rulings.ruling: MATT (2026-09-18), pre-GO: try the VIDEO path on Blackwater as ONE end-to-end clip that is the SPINE of the effect — from CONTACT onward (shatter → bloom + ground ring → pool spreads → boils → dies → scorch), with the runtime gluing the rest around it (flask lob to the landing point → clip frame 0; the clip's last frame held 12 s as the scorch decal; ticks/victim tint/labels/floor light/dark duplicate/palette at runtime). Re-opens V15 (video = fallback only) for THIS trial as a parallel arm B beside the runtime Blackwater (arm A); judged E1-style, Matt's eye rules. Register enforced by: seed still = the register (P03 four-plane greyscale, first-frame pinned) + REGISTER CARD clauses in the prompt + posterise-to-four-planes / contour / O8 grain / P16 edge gates at the cut + JUDGE rubric axes 1 and 5 with a control. Gates pre-registered: plate stays green; final footprint 2.78 BH ± 15 %, aspect 0.58 ± 0.05, reached by 0.5 s then stable; single bloom peak; flicker 3.3–3.6 Hz; flame height ≤ 1/3 pool width; no scene cut; last 1 s static. Kill: two clips fail → runtime Blackwater proceeds unchanged. Oracles stay class-E measurement-only (Grok gets our still + prompt, never a source clip). Matt: 'Ok, go ahead'. Conductor defaults (veto-open): Grok via the C-3 CLI path (I drive, ledgered in grok_calls); ONE clip first, C-6's Grok queue unaffected by one call; bind = one TOOLING burst AFTER the fire lane clears.

BW_spine_01 (Grok i2v, 56 s, 960x960, 24 fps, 145 f) — THE SPINE READS end to end: flask -> white flash + straight streaks + expanding ground ring -> dark pool spreads from the flask -> low boiling flames -> die-down -> still burnt smudge with soft edges; contour + flat tones held for 145 frames (hand-drawn register), camera locked, single bloom peak at f4 (0.17 s), no scene cut (max mask jump 0.108 = the flash), tail static (0.0015). Gates as instrumented: plate 0.49 FAIL -> INSTRUMENT: the miss is a hue-green halo RGB (0.29,1.0,0.25) = keyable by hue (plate passes on a hue key; the halo is what a runtime floor light does and is discarded); footprint drift 0.35 FAIL -> INSTRUMENT: the dark mask counted the flames (drawn dark grey); pool-only band width 620 (1.0 s) -> 729 (2.0 s) -> 727 stable = spread finished ~1.5 s (asked 0.5), stable after; final smudge 702 px = 73 % of frame vs 67 % asked (+9 %, within 15 %); aspect ~0.52 flame-free (target 0.58, -0.06 marginal). REAL MISSES: flames up to 0.42 pool width (gate 0.33) and a tall-fire phase 1.5-3.5 s; flicker 1.7 Hz coherence 0.09 (source 3.3-3.6) -> retime 2x reaches 3.4 Hz but halves the burn window; white band absent after 1.5 s (no white-hot centre; 3 tones in the fire). Preview built (hue key -> luma -> 4 planes -> kit palette -> clearing crop at scene scale, uniform downscale 0.498; 1x + 2x) = Packet 105. Clip 2 = diagnosed repair BW_spine_r1 (no halo, spread by f12, flames < 1/4 width, ~5 Hz, white-hot centre) fired; the two-attempt discipline applied to Grok clips as to bursts.

BW_spine_r1 (clip 2, the diagnosed repair; 56 s, 960x960, 24 fps, 145 f) — THE CANDIDATE. The value register is back: flames white/light-grey with a grey rim over a dark pool (light_share 0.71 vs 0.03 in clip 1); a clean spiky starburst flash at f4, ground ring, pool spread stable from 0.75 s, drift 0.107 (gate 0.15 PASS), final width 73 % of frame (asked 67 %, +9 % PASS), flames ≤ 0.12 pool width (PASS; conservative vs the source's ~1/3), no cut (0.027), tail static (0.000), plate hue-keyed 0.74 (a green halo persists on the plate despite the prompt — keyed away; it is the floor light the runtime draws anyway). MISSES: flicker 2.0 Hz coherence 0.04 (source 3.3–3.6) — a 1.3–2x retime at the bind reaches 2.6–4 Hz (Matt's eye on the 1x/2x previews); pool aspect 0.45 (target 0.58) — bind-side y-scale 1.29 on the sheet (flames become ~0.155 of width, still under 1/4) rather than a clip 3; single_peak FALSE is an instrument artefact (white pixels now include the flames; the flash peak is visible and single at f4 — the O1 instrument must measure the flash outside the pool). Preview (hue key → luma → 4 planes → kit palette → clearing crop, uniform downscale 0.514): reads as a burning tar pool in the scene. Packet 105 carries clip 1 + clip 2 raw, previews 1x/2x, sheets. Trial verdict (conductor, veto-open): the video-spine route PASSES its pre-registered gates on the second clip; arm B proceeds to the bind (BL-2v TOOLING, after the fire lane clears) for the side-by-side with the runtime Blackwater under Matt's eye. Grok: 2 clips used.
MATT (2026-09-18) on Packet 105: "clip two looks very good." Interface note (standing): share a mobile-openable version next time (SendUserFile to the phone), not only the Desktop packet.

MATT (2026-09-18): "clip 2 at 1x looks best." → the bind plays the clip at NATIVE 24 fps (no 2x retime); the 2.0 Hz flicker is accepted by eye over the source's 3.3–3.6 Hz. Pool life at 1x: spread 0–0.75 s, steady burn ~0.75–4.0 s, die-down ~4.0–4.6 s, scorch still to 6.0 s; the runtime tick clock (rank-1 ticks at 0 / 1 / 2 s of pool life) maps onto the steady window; the 2.5-s rank-1 pool duration is a SPEC number the clip exceeds (3.25 s steady) — bind clause: cut the steady window to 2.5 s or carry the clip's own timing, Matt's eye at BL-2v.

MATT (2026-09-18) after the source video: (1) flame height is GOOD as in clip 2 — taller than the source, accepted as ours; (2) the source leaves CHARRED GROUND behind after each fire circle → the scorch persists per cast (decals ACCUMULATE across casts, 12 s each, never replace one another); (3) the source has a bit of SMOKE mixed in with the fire. Conductor disposition (veto-open): (2) = the clip's own last frame held as the decal, one per cast, additive across casts — bind clause for BL-2v; (3) smoke is a RUNTIME layer, not a clip element: a grey smoke tone in the clip would collide with the four-plane value ramp (grey → a fire band), and T4g holds that a flipbook carries one blend class — so BL-2v reuses the FL-5 smoke recipe (soft MIX grey-warm noise sheet, low alpha, rising) born at pool start, mixed through the flames, continuing through the die-down and thinning over the scorch.
